questions.definition: A translator that converts assembly language into machine code.
questions.explanation: An assembler translates mnemonic assembly instructions into binary machine code that the processor can execute.

questions.definition: Code written in mnemonics that allows direct manipulation of hardware and must be converted into binary code to run.
questions.explanation: Assembly language is close to machine code but uses short mnemonic instructions that are easier for humans to read.

questions.definition: A feature of an editor that gives the user options when they start typing a command.
questions.explanation: Auto-completion can speed up programming and reduce typing errors by suggesting commands, variables, and functions.

questions.definition: A feature of an editor that identifies spelling errors and changes them.
questions.explanation: Auto-correction can correct common typing mistakes, though programmers must check that changes are appropriate.

questions.definition: A feature that allows sections of code, such as procedures, to be minimised so there is less code to read through.
questions.explanation: Block minimising helps programmers focus on relevant parts of a program by hiding sections they are not currently editing.

questions.definition: Points set by the user where the code stops running so values and output can be checked.
questions.explanation: Break points pause a program at chosen lines, allowing the programmer to inspect variables and program state.

questions.definition: A translator that converts a high-level language into a low-level language and checks all code before running the program.
questions.explanation: A compiler translates source code into machine code, often producing an executable file.

questions.definition: A file produced by a compiler that can be run independently of translator software and does not include the source code.
questions.explanation: Executable files contain translated machine code, so users can run the program without needing the original source code.

questions.definition: A type of programming language that uses English-like commands.
questions.explanation: High-level languages are easier for humans to read and write, but they must be translated before the CPU can execute them.

questions.definition: A piece of software that allows a user to write, test, and run program code.
questions.explanation: An IDE combines tools such as a code editor, translator, debugger, and run-time environment.

questions.definition: A translator that converts a high-level language into a low-level language one line at a time and executes each line before checking the next.
questions.explanation: Interpreters are useful during development because errors can be found as the program runs, but execution may be slower.

questions.definition: A language closer to the machine's language, such as assembly language or binary code.
questions.explanation: Low-level languages give more direct control over hardware but are harder for humans to read and write.

questions.definition: Binary code that is an example of a low-level language.
questions.clue: The CPU can execute this directly.
questions.explanation: Machine code consists of binary instructions that a processor can understand and run.

questions.definition: Instruction code used in assembly language.
questions.explanation: Mnemonics, such as ADD or LDA, represent machine code instructions in a form that is easier for programmers to remember.

questions.definition: A program that cannot be run on different types and manufacturers of computers.
questions.explanation: Non-portable software depends on specific hardware or operating systems and may need changes to run elsewhere.

questions.definition: A feature of an editor that changes the colour of text, for example to highlight keywords.
questions.explanation: Prettyprinting makes code easier to read by using formatting or colours to show keywords, strings, comments, and other elements.

questions.definition: A feature of an IDE that allows a program to be run and lets the user interact with it.
questions.explanation: The run-time environment provides the conditions needed to execute and test a program.

questions.definition: Running a program one line at a time in an IDE so it can be checked step by step.
questions.clue: Debug one line at a time.
questions.explanation: Stepping helps programmers trace program flow and inspect variable values after each instruction.

questions.definition: Software that converts code written in one programming language into another, usually from a high-level language into a low-level language.
questions.explanation: Translators allow source code written by humans to be converted into code that a computer can execute.

questions.definition: A debugging feature that displays variable values while code is running so they can be checked.
questions.explanation: A variable watch window helps programmers see how values change as a program executes.
